summary: Preliminary text audit of the current 6 English contrasts / 18 pairs and 4 German contrasts / 12 pairs. No definite word, IPA, category-order or phonemic-minimality correction was established. One existing pronunciation-dependent English pair remains an explicit review condition. Internal structural consistency passed for all 30 pairs, but selective dictionary checks and generated-session checks are not independent pronunciation approval. No curriculum, candidate or audio was modified; this document does not authorize audio regeneration or release.
checksPerformed: Read all current English and German contrast descriptions, word text, IPA, phoneme arrays, meanings, pair notes, stated dialects, sources and listening-group metadata in rescue/content/curriculum.json. Source SHA-256: 9e75f976f8b72d0df1f6b5da4c6afda06074d4f13ae91a533c0a77ebe7fe1db6.

Checked all 30 pairs for equal token lengths and exactly one phoneme-token substitution; the changed token matched the declared targetTokenIndex and ordered contrast categories. No inconsistency found. Affricate /dʒ/ and diphthongs were treated as the authored single phoneme tokens, not split Unicode characters.

Checked all 60 word IPA strings against their phoneme arrays after removing transcription slashes, stress and syllable marks. No mismatch found. This verifies internal transcription consistency, not dictionary attestation for every token.

Generated 25 real-engine sessions per contrast, 12 rounds per session: 250 sessions / 3,000 rounds. Checked distinct X lexical item and pair, compatible trial group and category, and distinct reference/test voices. No structural failures found. No audio was played or generated by this check.

Reviewed General American scope: the current English vowel, rhotic and consonant pairs are compatible with their selected broad forms. Omission of length marks on American tense vowels and /ɝ/ versus dictionary /ɜr/ are transcription conventions, not automatic errors. FOOT/STRUT is not asserted to cover every English dialect.

Checked the unusual English noun pledger against Collins / Webster’s New World: https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/pledger . The entry supports the noun and first-syllable-stressed American pronunciation; the current pleasure/pledger contrast is textually defensible.

Checked version and virgin against Collins / Webster’s New World American entries and Cambridge version pronunciations: https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/version ; https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/virgin ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/pronunciation/english/version . The selected shared-final-schwa readings are attested, while alternative final /ɪ/ in virgin and /ʃ/ in version require exclusion for this particular pair.

Reviewed Standard German as spoken in Germany scope and current citation-form caveats. The short /ʊ–ʏ/, quality-plus-length /ɪ–iː/, intervocalic /s–z/ and long /oː–øː/ pairs are internally phonemically minimal. Cross-word groups keep the target in the declared first stressed vowel or intervocalic consonant position; different word length across reference and X does not by itself break this category-matching task.

Checked German lexical and inflectional items selectively against publisher dictionary entries: https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/werden_Hilfsverb ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/reiszen ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Musze ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Muse ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Rohr ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Roehre ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/schon_bereits_eh_laengst ; https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/schoen . Duden explicitly exposes /ˈmuːsə/ for Muße and /ˈrøːrə/ for Röhre. Publisher notation /r/ versus the curriculum broad /ʁ/ does not establish a segmental mismatch. The current Rohre/Röhre plural-versus-singular and rote/Röte inflectional notes correctly identify different grammatical forms rather than claiming shared morphology.

Limit: several Duden pages expose lexical entries but no machine-readable IPA, and the linked Kohler German illustration DOI did not resolve through the browsing tool during this bounded pass. Exact pronunciation evidence was therefore selective; no claim is made that every German word was freshly verified against a complete pronunciation dictionary, or that any existing recording follows its declared form.

Inspected isolated candidate artifact IDs without incorporating or linguistically approving them: English batches 2–5 contain 18 absent-from-current contrasts / 54 pairs; French legacy batches 3–5 contain 8 absent-from-current contrasts / 24 pairs. French /u–y/ depth candidate separately contains 2 practice sets / 6 pairs for an existing contrast, not 2 new phonemic contrasts. French legacy batch 2 and 2 of the 3 batch-3 contrasts are already current and were not counted as isolated expansions.

findings.message: This is an attested but pronunciation-dependent minimal pair, not a dialect-independent one. The current /ˈvɝʒən/–/ˈvɝdʒən/ selects shared final schwa. Collins also lists virgin with final /ɪ/ and version with /ʃ/. Either alternative would violate this pair’s declared target-only difference. The current description, note and ABX caution already state this restriction; their existence does not demonstrate that a generated or recorded voice follows it.
findings.suggestedCorrection: No mandatory textual replacement established. Preserve the selected-reading caveat and treat this pair as conditional in the text inventory. Before any eventual recording acceptance, review each voice for /ʒ/ in version and the same final schwa in both words; exclude a mismatching token instead of assuming its spelling guarantees the target. This audit grants no audio-generation or release approval.
